abstract: In helical X-ray computed tomography (CT) imaging, under sampling in the z-axis direction will cause windmill artifacts, leading to serious image quality degradation and mistakes in diagnosis. In this paper, a method based on dual-domain filtering and improved distance transform is proposed to reduce the windmill artifacts in helical CT images. In this study, firstly CT projection data are generated by simulation and the helical CT images with windmill artifacts are reconstructed by the FDK reconstruction algorithm. Then, the reduction effect of windmill artifacts is analyzed by using bilateral filtering kernel of different radius. Finally, the kernel radius is adjusted according to the improved distance transform to reduce the windmill artifacts. In this study, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method are preliminarily verified by computer simulation experiments. The proposed method can retain the details in the images of the scanned objects while reducing windmill artifacts in the helical CT images. We will further validate the performance of the proposed method in a real helical CT in the future.

articleTitle: A Suppression Method Against C&I Jamming by Time-frequency Shift Recombination
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Chopping and Interleaving jamming (C&I) is an effective jamming method against linear frequency modulated (LFM) pulse compression radar. In order to suppress the false target generated by C&I jamming, a method based on time-frequency shift recombination is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the jamming signals received are analyzed by Gabor transform, and then the number of chopping and the number of interleaving are estimated. After that, the modulated signals are designed based on the key jamming parameters to carry out time-frequency shift and recombination. Finally, the jamming was suppressed by matched filtering. The simulation results show that the proposed method can effectively utilize the energy of the jamming signal, solve the problem that it is difficult to suppress the jamming when the jamming to signal ratio (JSR) is relatively large, and avoid the complicated signal separation algorithm. When the JSR is 10dB, the signal to jamming plus noise ratio gain can reach more than 20dB after jamming suppression.

articleTitle: Improved Collaborative Filtering Recommendation Algorithm Adapted to User Interest Change
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Collaborative filtering algorithm is the most widely used algorithm in the recommendation system. Its core is to recommend the target according to the neighbor users or similar items. When the traditional collaborative filtering algorithm is faced with sparse data, the computational similarity accuracy is low, which indirectly leads to the quality decline of the recommendation system. To alleviate the influence of data sparsity on similarity calculation and improve recommendation quality, an improved collaborative filtering recommendation algorithm adapted to the change of user interest is proposed. Firstly, considering the user preference similarity, the traditional cosine similarity is combined with the penalty factor of popular items, while the correction factor for the user rating score difference degree and the user rating tendency similarity are introduced; then, for the user interest decay problem, the Ebbinghaus forgetting function is incorporated into the Pearson correlation coefficient and modified using the common scoring weighting function. Finally, the correlations between user preferences and user interest changes are obtained by weighted fusion, to calculate more accurate user similarity. The experimental results show that the algorithm of this paper effectively improves the prediction accuracy of the recommendation system.

articleTitle: Bearing Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Improved Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: A bearing fault diagnosis method based on an improved convolutional neural network(CNN) is proposed to address the problem of low accuracy of traditional convolutional neural network for rolling bearing fault identification. First, the convolutional kernels of the first convolutional layer of the original network are widened to accommodate the bearing fault signal with one-dimensional input. Then, the number of convolutional kernels is reduced while maintaining the feature extraction capability of the network to ensure the deepening of the network while strongly suppressing the overfitting phenomenon of the network. Finally, the batch normalization(BN) layer is added after the convolutional and fully connected layers of the convolutional neural network to accelerate the convergence of the network and prevent the network from gradient disappearance or gradient explosion. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves higher diagnostic accuracy and stability than traditional convolutional neural network.

articleTitle: De-noising Method for Fiber Optic Gyroscope Based on VMD-PE-CMSE
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: To improve the short-term precision of inertial navigation system(INS), the noise of the inertial measurement(IMU) should be de-noised. In order to reduce the noise of the Fiber Optic Gyroscope, variational mode decomposition(VMD) combined with permutation entropy(PE) and Consecutive Mean Square Error(CMSE) is utilized in the de-noise method. The raw signal is decomposed into the intrinsic mode functions(IMFs) by VMD, the noise of IMF can be identified by PE, and the IMF is de-noised by CMSE. The reconstructed signal is composed of de-noised IMFs. The result of the experiments show that VMD combined with PE can identify the noise of the signal, and CMSE can de-noise the signal effectively. The static test show that the de-noising method can improve the short-term precision of INS.

articleTitle: A Method for Evaluating Surface Deformation Error of Mesh Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The surface deformation of the mesh reflector antenna is an important factor affecting the electrical performance of the antenna. Generally, the electrical performance of the antenna is evaluated by the root mean of the surface deformation error. Affected by various errors, the evaluation results are inconsistent with the actual performance. In order to further improve the evaluation accuracy and improve the electrical performance evaluation results, this paper proposes a novel evaluation method. The information entropy is used to evaluate error distribution of surface deformation error and the nearest neighbor index is used to evaluate spatial distribution of surface deformation error, so as to realize the electrical performance evaluation of mesh reflector antenna. Experimental results show that the proposed method is effective and reliable. The method can improve the electrical performance evaluation results from high accuracy.

articleTitle: Condition-based maintenance strategy for assembly line equipment based on Gamma process approach
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Taking the equipment of assembly line as an example, this paper proposes a condition-based maintenance strategy based on Gamma rules. For the single equipment and the same type of dual-equipment in the assembly line, considering the continuous degradation of the equipment. The corresponding maintenance behavior is determined through the detection of the equipment state, and the system maintenance decision is made. Taking the cost rate during system operation as the target, the cost rate model of the system is established. Through the theoretical derivation and numerical solution of the probability density function of the equipment state, the maintenance probability of a single-equipment system and the same type of dual-equipment system under different maintenance behaviors is calculated. The genetic algorithm is used to optimize the maintenance decision optimization model, and the optimization results of the single-equipment system and the same type of dual-equipment system are obtained.

articleTitle: Research on Power Transform Technology of High Resolution Range Profile of Measured Ship
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: This paper mainly studies the power transform preprocessing of High Resolution Range Profile (HRRP). Power transform can make the HRRP data tend to be normally distributed, improve the recognition effect of common classifiers such as linear discriminant function and k-nearest neighbor (KNN), increase the role of weak scattered points in recognition, and weaken the shielding effect of strong scattered points on weak scattered points, so as to alleviate the attitude sensitivity problem of HRRP. This paper first introduces the statistical properties of HRRP, then introduces the properties of power transform and parameter estimation methods, including parameter estimation based on the skewness and kurtosis normality test and Jarque-Bera normality test. After analyzing and summarizing the shortcomings of the two methods, the parameter estimation method of adaptive Jarque-Bera normality test was proposed. The power transform parameters obtained from the improved parameter estimation method of Jarque-Bera normality test were used to preprocess the measured HRRP. The results were verified by normplot and the measured ship HRRP, which are more close to the normal distribution; In the meantime, the target classification and recognition experiment is carried out by using the measured ship HRRP data after power transform, and the average recognition accuracy is improved by more than 4.8 percent.

articleTitle: Robust Stability of Switched Logical Networks with Function Perturbation under Arbitrary Switching Signals
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In genetic regulatory networks, the analysis for function perturbation of switched logical networks (SLNs) is an important issue. This paper investigates robust stability of SLNs with function perturbation under arbitrary switching signals. By using the semi-tensor product of matrices, the equivalent algebraic expression of SLNs is established, and one necessary and sufficient condition for global stability of SLNs under arbitrary switching signals is proposed. After function perturbation, system is still globally stable under arbitrary switching signals if and only if the intersection of two index sets is an empty set. Finally, an illustrative example is given to demonstrate the obtained results.

articleTitle: A closed-loop FDSST algorithm based on SVM
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The open-loop nature of target trackers makes them susceptible to degradation caused by background interference and hence target loss. To solve this problem, an improved closed-loop tracking algorithm based on Fast Discriminative Scale Space Tracker (FDSST) is proposed in this paper. The algorithm uses SVM to build a verification module to verify the tracking results, and outputs tracking state information with a state machine. The system uses different update rate adjustment strategies for different states to reduce the impact of background on the tracker. When the target is lost the re-detection module built from the SVM is activated, thus the system has closed-loop characteristics. The results on the OTB50 dataset show that the algorithm outperforms some mainstream algorithms in both success rate and distance accuracy, and has strong resistance to occlusion. The tests on the Hi3559A platform show that the algorithm has great real-time performance.

articleTitle: Learning from Noisy Labeled Data via Sharpen Prediction Loss and Re-Correction
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Deep learning has achieved excellent results in many applications with a large number of high-quality annotation datasets. However, it is difficult to obtain numerous high-quality labeled samples, since it may generate noisy labeled data during manually annotating. Deep neural network with noisy labeled data leads to overfitting a nd greatly affects t he performance. In order to overcome the issue, a deep model with sharpen prediction loss and re-correction is proposed for learning from noisy labeled data, which aims to modify the loss distributions of noise samples and clean samples, and eliminate noise samples by unsupervised clustering. In the proposed framework, the deep model is warmed up through several epochs, sharpen prediction loss is proposed to effectively measure the sample loss, and recorrection is utilized to separate noise and clean samples as well as predict the final l abels. Experimental results on two datasets with noisy labeled data demonstrate that our proposed model yields superior classification accuracies.

articleTitle: Path planning and hunting control of multiple dynamic targets based on event-triggered strategy
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Aiming at the path planning and hunting control problem of multiple dynamic targets in a first-order nonlinear system, an algorithm based on an event-triggered strategy is proposed: the path planning process first uses the Kalman tracking algorithm to obtain the target state estimation, and then design the controller Control the multi agent to track and generate the path according to the estimation of the target. This article uses matrix theory, graph theory and Lyapunov stability methods to obtain the conditions for system stability. The whole round-up process is divided into three stages. The first is the cruise stage, where multiple agents maintain their leadership and follow the formation to cruise and move. The second is the pre round up stage. When the distance between the agent and the target is less than a certain value, an event is triggered. Pre round up, and the third is final round-up. The event is triggered after maintaining the pre round up formation for a certain period of time, and the round-up range is reduced to achieve round-up. Simulation experiments show that the event triggered joint path planning and hunting control algorithm enables the multi agent system to form and maintain multiple hunting formations to hunt multiple dynamic targets, and realize the hunting of multiple dynamic targets.

Author Keywords: Target dynamic path planning and round-up

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional ISAR Imaging with Pattern-Coupled Sparse Structure Based on 2D-RFISTA
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In order to improve the imaging quality of two-dimensional inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) under the conditions of low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and sparsity rate (SR), in view of pattern-coupled sparse structure (PCSS) of the imaging target, a novel two-dimensional joint sparse imaging algorithm, namely two-dimensional reweighted fast iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm (2D-RFISTA) is proposed. One dimensional RFISTA (1D-RFISTA) is extended to 2D-RFISTA by matrix processing and design of the pattern-coupled mode, which reduces the complexity of the algorithm and improves the imaging performance under noisy and sparse conditions. Experimental results based on measured data demonstrate that the proposed algorithm has excellent imaging quality and is suitable for the imaging scene with low time requirement.

Author Keywords: two-dimensional reweighted fast iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm

articleTitle: Modified Lanczos Algorithm for L2,1 norm Regularization Extreme Learning Machine
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: It is known that L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,1</inf> norm regularization extreme learning machine (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,1</inf>-RELM) has strong robustness and good generalization performance in most cases. Though fitting problems had been solved, L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,1</inf>-RELM also exists high computational complexity. To solve this problem, a modified Lanczos algorithm is proposed for L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,1</inf>-RELM through iteration to compute output weights, and low computational complexity and fast convergence rate is achieved. Experimental results on artificial datasets and real benchmark datasets show that the proposed algorithm obtains better robustness and higher learning speed than ELM, RELM, Lan-ELM in most cases.

articleTitle: High-Precision Micro-motion Parameter Estimation of Sparse Aperture Ballistic Target
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The discontinuity of target echo data under sparse aperture (SA) observation will make it difficult to extract micromotion parameters. To address this problem, this paper proposes a novel method for high-precision micro-motion curve reconstruction of ballistic targets with sparse aperture. For the complex phase modulation of ballistic target echo, the proposed method adopts the idea of piecewise, and a simplified echo signal model is established through the quantitative analysis. Combined with the modified CLEAN algorithm, the phase information of high-resolution range profile (HRRP) is used to estimate the micro-motion curve parameters of each scattering center. The estimation accuracy can reach the level of half a wavelength, and the phase unwrapping can be avoided, so as to the high-precision micro-motion curve can be obtained. Extensive experimental results are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Impulsive Sequence Design for Finite-Time Set Stabilization of Impulsive Probabilistic Boolean Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: This paper studies the impulsive sequence design for finite-time set stabilization with probability one of impulsive probabilistic Boolean networks (IPBNs). Firstly, the equivalent algebraic form of IPBNs is obtained by using the semi-tensor product (STP) method. Secondly, the design of impulsive sequence is converted to the design of state feedback control. Thirdly, based on the concept of control-invariant subset with impulsive sequence (CISIS), a necessary and sufficient condition is put forward to solve the finite-time set stabilization with probability one. Finally, an example is given to demonstrate the obtained results.

articleTitle: Visual tracking based on multi-cue framework and hierarchical aggregation
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Existing Siamese network based trackers define target tracking as a similarity matching problem between the initial template and search regions. However, the initial template contains extremely limited target information that ignores appearance variations over time. Aiming at this problem, a visual tracking method based on multi-cue framework and hierarchical aggregation is proposed in this paper. Firstly, we put forward a stability evaluation mechanism to select the stable template for similarity matching, so that the tracker can adapt to the target appearance changes. Secondly, we construct a multi-cue tracking framework combining the initial template branch and the stable template branch for parallel tracking, thus solving the single template limitation. Finally, we propose a hierarchical aggregation strategy that combines complementary merits to further improve tracking performance. Comprehensive experimental results on the benchmark dataset demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves favorable tracking performance.

articleTitle: Indoor scene classification model based on multi-modal fusion
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Aiming at the classification of indoor scene images, a multi-modal fusion model is proposed. Firstly, based on the scene image and its semantic description, a single-modal classification model is constructed. For scene images, a convolutional neural network is used to extract features and train classification models. For scene semantic descriptions, a recurrent neural network is used to extract text features. A scene feature space is then constructed and the semantic descriptions are embedded to it to obtain classification results. Secondly, these two kinds of single-modal features are fused and input to a deep neural network after dimensionality reduction, a feature-level fusion model is trained. Finally, two single-modal models and the feature-level fusion model are given different weights to construct a hybrid fusion model, the weights are constantly adjusted to get the best classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Exponential Stabilization of Chaotic Neural Networks via aperiodic Sampled-data Control
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In this paper, the exponential stabilization problem is investigated for chaotic neural networks under aperiodic sampled-data control. Firstly, a novel time-dependent Lyapunov functional is proposed for closed-loop system. The main advantage of the constructed Lyapunov functional lies in that it takes full advantage of the states information over the sampling intervals. With the aid of Lyapunov stability theory and some inequality estimation techniques, some sufficient stabilization criteria are established for the chaotic system. Moreover, the desired sampled-data controller is designed by solving a group of linear matrix inequalities. Lastly, two numerical simulation examples are given to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Adaptive observer design for a multi-model subject to unknown inputs and outputs with unmeasurable decision variables
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: This paper addresses the design of an adaptive observer for nonlinear systems exposed to unknown inputs and outputs. The Takagi-Sugeno multimodel approach is proposed to transform the complex nonlinear model to an interpolation of simple linear models with unmeasurable premise variables. Then a mathematical transformation is used to represent the unknown outputs as unknown inputs. This work is based on a proportional integral unknown input observer in order to provide the state and the faults estimation for the considered system. The exponential stability conditions are studied with the L2 optimization and Lyapunov function, and obtained by solving linear matrix inequalities (LMI). Finally, to show the effectiveness of the proposed observer, a numerical simulation is carried out on a hydraulic system.

articleTitle: Formulation of Relationship in Bibliographic Networks Using Follow Model of Micro-Blogging
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Follow Model as one of a few mathematical models for Micro-Blogging has been developed with 10 years. In the study of bibliographic networks, we propose an alternative logical formulation using Follow Model to describe the paper citation relationship. With this formulation, we interpret some scenarios of human social activities such as: if an author cites many papers of the authors from a group, he may also cite the paper of another author who is a relative of this group. We propose the citation prediction and query methods for bibliographic networks just as the similar activities in On-line Social Networks. By means of finding the citations of a book by Tim Berners-Lee and Mark Fischetti, the recommended model shows to be effective and efficient even in more sophisticated queries.

articleTitle: GRSiamFC: Group Residual Convolutional Siamese Networks for Object Tracking
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Visual tracking has seen considerable success with fully convolutional Siamese networks (SiamFC). However, the features extracted by SiamFC are redundant in practical applications. Most of the feature channels are ineffective or even serve as noise, which adversely affects tracking performance. The convolutional kernels tend to converge during the training phase of SiamFC, thereby the output features are typically redundant or irrelevant. In this paper, we propose a group residual convolutional Siamese network (GRSiamFC) to address this problem. Specifically, GRSiamFC divides the convolutional layers used for feature extraction into groups and trains each group in turn. Then the residuals between the output of previous groups and the true labels are used as losses to guide the current group to learn the residuals that were not fitted by the previous group, thereby improving the discriminative ability of the model. Extensive experiments on OTB50, OTB100, UAV123, and UAV20L show that the proposed GRSiamFC significantly improves the performance of SiamFC while keeping the complexity unchanged.

articleTitle: An Iterative Algorithm Design for Radar-Communication Coexistence
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In this paper, we consider and analyze a novel spectrum sharing framework for the joint design of a colocated MIMO radar and a MIMO communication system wherein both radar transceiver and communication transmitter designs are investigated, in which the filtered effective radar interference power is minimized under the transmit power, similarity, and the mutual information (MI) for communication system requirement. In order to solve the original non-convex problem effectiveness, an alternating iterative algorithm is exploited for the derived multi-subproblems. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed spectrum sharing approach is demonstrated by numerical results.

articleTitle: Anomalous behavior detection of vessels based on shore-based radar data
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: It is a consensus that anomalous behavior detection of marine vessels is critical for improving navigation efficiency and ensuring navigation safety. However, most conventional researches focused on the vessels sailing on a river or sea, where the intersection area of rivers is not highly concerned. In this paper, a novel method, which uses shore-based radar to obtain the position data of vessels in the intersecting area of rivers, is proposed to detect vessel anomalous behavior. Based on the shore-based radar data, we establish the definition model of judgment regions and the detection model of vessels behavior to detect different degrees of violation behavior of vessels entering and leaving the estuary of Liuwei. Compared with the traditional method based on the AIS data, the proposed method in this paper achieves higher accuracy and better engineering applicability.

articleTitle: A Robotic Device For Measuring Alignment Of Elevator Guide Rails
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low degree of automation, troublesome technical measurement method and low efficiency in the current elevator track deformation detection method, a high degree of automation elevator track quality detection robot is designed and developed in this paper. The robot fully considers practicability and high efficiency in mechanical design and adds a feedback mechanism to the control unit for control optimization, so that it can climb the elevator track quickly and smoothly, and uses robot vision to detect the track deformation, main control principle is to use the computer to smoothly regulate the speed of the motor, to detect the posture of the robot in the climbing process in real-time, and to feed it back to the micro industrial computer for autonomous adjustment, to ensure that the robot runs smoothly on the elevator guide rail at all times.

articleTitle: A New Semantic Segmentation Network with FPFN and Dense ASPP
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the DeepLabv3+ network does not fully use the multi-scale feature information generated by the backbone network and the excessive atrous rate in the atrous spatial pyramid pooling (ASPP) leads to poor segmentation results for small targets, the FPDA DeepLabv3+ network is proposed. First, the backbone network was replaced with MobileNetv3 to reduce the number of model parameters, and then the ASPP connection method was changed to a dense connection to capture a larger receptive field. Finally, the Feature Pyramid Fusion Network (FPFN) was used to integrate the high-resolution features effectively. The experimental results show that the mIoU and mPA of the FPDA DeepLabv3+ network on the semantic segmentation data set AeroScapes verification set reached 82.98% and 91.36%, respectively, which fully verified that the network could effectively improve the prediction results on the data set AeroScapes.

articleTitle: Otsu algorithm based on adaptive Kalman filter
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the traditional Otsu algorithm cannot segment the image well under the condition of illumination and background interference and the traditional Kalman filter performs poorly in predicting the position of nonlinear targets, an Otsu algorithm based on adaptive Kalman filter is proposed. In this algorithm, the Kalman gain is adjusted online to make the filter quickly and smoothly predict the trajectory of nonlinear targets accurately, and the area of background and shadow area is reduced by setting the focus area. At the same time, in order to reduce the area of the focus area and ensure that the target is always in the region, the focus area is placed in the target position predicted by the adaptive Kalman filter. The experimental results show that compared with the traditional algorithm, the image segmentation performance of this algorithm is significantly improved.

articleTitle: Cooperative Transmit Resource Optimization and Waveform Selection Strategy for Target Tracking in Multiple Radars System
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In this paper, a cooperative transmit resource optimization and waveform selection (CTROWS) strategy is developed for target tracking in multiple radars system. The main aim of the proposed strategy is to improve the low probability of intercept (LPI) performance and target tracking accuracy of the underlying system while satisfying the transmit resource budgets and waveform library limitation, where the probability of intercept and Bayesian Cramér-Rao Lower Bound (BCRLB) are utilized to evaluate the LPI performance and target tracking accuracy, respectively. It is shown that the resulting problem is a complex dual-objective and NP-hard optimization problem, where the four involved parameters, i.e., the transmit power, dwell time, waveform bandwidth, and pulse length, are all coupled in the objective functions and constraints. Combined with the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm, we propose an efficient and fast three-step solution technique to solve the above optimization model. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of our proposed optimization strategy compared with other existing algorithms.

Author Keywords: Cooperative transmit resource optimization and waveform selection (CTROWS)

articleTitle: Orthogonal Matching Pursuit DOA Estimation for Nested Arrays in Non-Gaussian Clutter
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The nested array has attracted considerable attention in the field of array signal processing because of increasing the degree of freedom (DOF). However, most of these technologies assume that white Gaussian noise is used in ideal conditions. This paper considers the problem of direction of arrival (DOA) estimation in cyclic non-Gaussian clutter modeled as a complex symmetric α stable (SaS) process. Combining the theory of phased fractional low-order moment (PFLOM) and compressed sensing, we propose an orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) DOA estimation algorithm named OMP-NA-PFLOM based on a nested array. The advantage of the proposed method is that it preserves the array aperture and has better DOA estimation performance. Simulation results show that the proposed method is superior to previously reported algorithms.

articleTitle: Polynomial Lyapunov Functions for Consensus of Multi-agent Systems via PD control
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: This paper investigates the consensus problem of multi-agent systems under the proportional-derivative (PD) control protocol. It devises an automatic search algorithm for the polynomial Lyapunov functions beyond the conventional quadratic form. With a relaxation of Lipschitz-like condition, a criterion is established for consensus of multi-agent systems via the PD control. Then, the relaxed nonnegativity conditions can be transformed into the sum-of-squares conditions for polynomial systems. And the polynomial Lyapunov functions are then obtained by solving the sum-of-squares optimization problem within the convex programming framework, which can be addressed efficiently in polynomial time. Finally, a numerical example is presented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: State Estimation for the Unknown Motion Model with Bearing-only Measurement
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: This paper presents the problem of state estimation for moving objects with bearing-only measurements in the case that the a priori motion model is unknown, i.e., its acceleration is absolutely unknown, which can not be dealt with by the mainstream Kalman-like schemes based on the known motion model. First, the essential reason disadvantage of the bearing-only measurement in the states estimation is described, and hence an alternative measurement is proposed. Then, an unknown input observer is proposed to estimate the position and velocity of the object. Finally, the numeric simulation demonstrates the effectiveness in terms of estimation accuracy and terminative time.

articleTitle: A Gradient-based Event-Triggered MPC for Perturbed Linear Systems: Control Performance and Safety Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In this paper, we put forward a gradient-based event-triggered model predictive control (ET-MPC) strategy to linear systems subject to constraints as well as additive disturbances. The triggering condition of the proposed method is constructed on the basis of the error gradients between the real states and the best prediction trajectories at two consecutive sampling moments, as well as a tightening robust constraint designed against the disturbances in the system. Then, the resilience property of the proposed ET-MPC against denial-of-service (DoS) is analyzed and the maximum safety duration is derived. In addition, sufficient conditions guaranteeing the feasibility of the new ET-MPC algorithm, and the closed-loop stability are provided. Finally, the simulations and comparisons are performed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Event-triggered Stability Analysis for Linear Systems with Time-delay Based on Sampled-Data
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In this paper, the finite-time stability (FTS) and finite-time contractive stability (FTCS) are considered for linear time-delay system via sampled-data-based event-triggered control. By using the Lyapunov-Razumikhin method, several Lyapunov-based sufficient conditions are presented for establishing these FTS and FTCS properties. Finally, a numerical example illustrates the validity of the proposed results.

articleTitle: Mutual information estimation in Distributed data fusion
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: A crucial problem of data fusion in distributed sensor networks mainly results from the unknown correlation in the fusion process. With unknown correlation, the common process noises may cause double-counting errors in fusion results. To optimize the fusion results, the common process noises should be eliminated in fusion results. In this paper, the correlation from common process noises are modeled as the mutual part of two estimates. The size of the mutual part is qualified with information entropy, and then the value range of the mutual part is also analyzed with the joint entropy. Finally, the mutual part is estimated to optimize the fusion results and eliminated with covariance intersection. The simulation of target position verifies the improvement of the proposed fusion method compared to the current alternatives.

articleTitle: Effect of V-Groove positioning error on coupling loss
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Y-waveguide plays an important role in the information processing of optic fiber communication. The coupling of the optical fiber and waveguide is a key step of modulator packaging and it directly affects the inserting loss of the modulator. In this paper, the optical power loss caused by the V-groove positioning error was studied, and the causes of coupling losses were theoretically analyzed. The coupling efficiency of waveguide and fiber was calculated by using the three-dimensional model field overlap integral. Coupling loss caused by lateral error and longitudinal error was shown in this paper. The analysis results show that the Z-direction spacing within 0-3um has little effect on the coupling efficiency, and the power drop caused by the X-direction deviation is greater than that of the Y-direction deviation. It provides theoretical guidance for the coupling and packaging of multi-channel Y-waveguides.

articleTitle: Research on the Algorithm of Power Allocation in the Integrated Radar and Communication System
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The integrated radar and communication system has become a research hotspot in recent years due to its advantages of high utilization of hardware equipment and spectrum. For the application requirement of the integrated radar and communication system, a power allocation algorithm based on spectrum sharing is proposed. Firstly, we establish a signal model of integrated radar and communication system. Then, the evaluation index of radar performance based on mutual information between the random target impulse response and the received radar signal is constructed, and an optimization model with the goal of maximizing mutual information and channel capacity is constructed. Finally, combined with the KKT condition derivation, it utilizes the block coordinate descent method to find optimal solution iteratively. Simulation results show that under the given constraints, the power allocation algorithm proposed in this paper can effectively improve system performance.

articleTitle: An Iterative Ensemble Transform Kalman Filter Based on the Smoothing and the Filtering Steps
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: For nonlinear systems, the performance of traditional filtering algorithms is generally not very good, so we consider using the observation information to implement a smoothing step before the forecasting step. In this article we propose a smoothing iterative formulation of the ensemble transform Kalman filter (SIETKF) in the perfect-model, which is similar to the iterative ensemble Kalman filter (IEnKF -S) by Sakov and Oliver. First we propose a two-step (the smoothing and the filtering steps) framework of the data assimilation. Specifically, we collect the observation information at the current moment, which is used to smooth the state at the previous moment (i.e., the smoothing step), and then complete the filtering based on the observation information and the new smooth state (i.e., the filtering step). Next, inflation is further implemented to improve the robustness of the algorithm and to decrease the sample errors. We compare the performance of the proposed algorithm with other algorithms in 3-element and 40-element Lorenz models. The experimental results show that our algorithm performs better than two traditional algorithms. In particularly, for the strong nonlinear model, it outperforms the algorithm that uses the observation information at the next moment (IEnKF -S).

articleTitle: Evidence Combination Based on Belief Interval
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The theory of belief functions is widely used in the field of multi-source information fusion, where the combination rule of evidence is used to combine evidences from different information sources. However, Dempster's rule of combination might have some counter-intuitive behaviors, which hinders its practical applications. In this paper, we propose an indirect evidence combination method using belief intervals of focal elements. The fused belief interval is obtained through some operations for interval, and then the combined evidence is obtained from the fused belief interval with the uncertainty optimization. Results of numerical examples and experiments show that the new evidence combination method is rational and can avoid the counter-intuitive results of Dempster's rule.

articleTitle: The Depth feature adaptive fusion vision tracking algorithm based on game theory
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Multi-feature fusion in convolutional neural network can effectively improve the robustness of visual tracking algorithm, but how to carry out multi-feature fusion is a key problem. Aiming at this problem, this paper proposes a depth feature adaptive fusion visual tracking algorithm based on game theory. Firstly, VGG19 network is used to extract the shallow and deep features of the target, and then the game theory is used to continuously game the shallow and deep features to give full play to the advantages of each feature to achieve a balanced state, and finally get the tracking results of the target. In order to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithm, the proposed algorithm is compared with other popular visual tracking algorithms on OTB100 and TC128 datasets respectively, the experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively improve the tracking success rate and accuracy, and has obvious advantages in fast motion, motion blur and other attributes.

articleTitle: Metal Mine Monitoring System Design
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a metal mine monitoring system, describing the architecture of the system design and focusing on the hardware and software design of its main node, the base station, which can test environmental parameters such as temperature and humidity, harmful gas concentration, wind speed, etc., and can transmit them to the monitoring centre via a hybrid wired and wireless network. The field test has achieved good results and is of great relevance to the construction of the six systems in the mine.

articleTitle: Efficiency analysis technique via time series network for the historical stage division of influenza information in China
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Influenza viruses are serious threat to human health in current society. The epidemic features of influenza viruses can be obtained effectively from the statistics of each historical stage. Complex networks theories are reliable tools to handle the issues of historical information division. In this paper, we propose an analysis technique to divide the historical stages of influenza information. Primarily, influenza networks are established using a visibility graph model. After that, the modules of networks are uncovered using the Arenas, Fernández and Gómez algorithm. Finally, on the basis of the clustering results, historical information of influenza virus can be reasonably divided into several stages. The simulations provide some conclusions. Time series networks are established reasonably, which can obtain a better results. The number of stages is reduced rationally, which is beneficial to gather the influenza information. Unreasonable statistics are avoided effectively, and some critical periods affecting the number of influenza like illness can be discovered.

articleTitle: Infrared Dim and Small Target detection based on sample data
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of high false alarm rate of infrared small target detection, a detection method of identifying infrared small target by using sample database is proposed. Firstly, according to the imaging characteristics of infrared small target, the background prediction algorithm is used to judge whether it is a suspected target pixel by pixel; Then, according to the prior sample data of the target and background, the random forest algorithm is used to train the classifier, and the classifier is used to make a second decision on the suspected target points to further filter out the false target points; Finally, according to the background sample data marked in the current scene, the false target points in the background are filtered out by using NCC similarity measure, and the final detection result is the infrared small target. Experiments show that this method can effectively reduce the false alarm rate of infrared small target detection, and can be used for infrared small target detection in strong clutter environment.

articleTitle: The design of Temperature detecting and Tracking system based on image recognition
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The temperature detecting and tracking system is designed for epidemic prevention. The system adopts the dual-core architecture and various data processing algorithms. There are three parts that includes non-contact temperature detection, pattern recognition and intelligent body tracking in the system. By using of non-contact infrared temperature measurement and median average filtering algorithm,the system realize real-time temperature measurement, and the highest temperature target is selected and locked, whose image is processed by means of OpenMV & the three frames subtraction, and whose location information is acquired by use of AprilTag 3D location & data fusion method, at the same time, via a serial port, the location information is sent to Mecanum-wheel control module of the car. Finally, the highest temperature target is real-time tracked. The system runs/works steadily and accurately, providing a solution for the current epidemic prevention and detection.

articleTitle: A Novel Cluster-Sorting Method for Radar Signals Based on Graph Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of traditional clustering algorithms that require manual screening of features, only learn the attribute information of the input signal, and have poor results in radar signal sorting. In this paper, a novel cluster-sorting method for radar signals based on Graph Autoencoder (GAE) is proposed. The key of this method is to obtain the adjacency matrix of the radar signal data by using the K nearest neighbor (KNN) algorithm, and then obtain the graph structure representation of the radar signals. The low-dimensional vector embedding is obtained after Graph Autoencoder learns the relevant information of the graph. Next the K-Means method is applied to the clustering of low-dimensional vector embedding, and the cluster-sorting of radar signals are completed. Finally, the proposed algorithm is compared with five typical clustering algorithms. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm is better than the typical method in radar signal cluster-sorting, and the signal sorting accuracy is higher 12.5%.

articleTitle: Extended Object Tracking Using Random Matrix with Adaptive Gate
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Extended object tracking is a field considering the kinematic state and the shape parameters of moving objects. In real radar processing, a main challenge in object tracking is that the measurements are not strictly follow certain distribution, because distance,human posture or surrounding environment all have effluence on measurements. In this paper, the random matrix with adaptive gate is introduced for multiple extended object tracking. The adaptive gate is efficient in data association which matches the JPDA method, and it is derived from the volume of ellipsoid and the amount of innovation the new measurement adds to an existing track. Single object and two objects scenario are analyzed, and numerical experiments based on simulation data are performed to test the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Compared with the random matrix with constant gate approach and JPDA method, the proposed method has great performance. The accuracy of this method is evaluated respectively by the RMSE and OSPA metric in single object tracking scenarios.

articleTitle: An Improved Speech Recognition System Based on Transformer Language Model
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: With the application of deep learning in speech recognition technology, many neural network-based model structures have emerged in speech recognition, while as another important part of language models, traditional statistical language models have not been further developed due to drawbacks such as oversized parameters, purely based on statistical frequencies, and poor generalization ability. To address those drawbacks, this paper uses a fully convolutional deep neural network-based acoustic model, which is then combined with a connected temporal classification method to replace the traditional statistical language model with a Transformer-based language model. Experiments on several datasets such as THCHS30 show that the recognition effectiveness of the Transformer-based language model speech recognition system is effectively improved.

articleTitle: A Real-time and Robust Image Matching Algorithm Using Inertial Information in Dynamic Environment
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: This paper proposes a tightly coupled visual-IMU odometry. Before fusing visual and inertial measurements, a real time and robust image matching algorithm which is based on inertial information is proposed. Delaunay triangulation and three consecutive image matching method are employed to remove sporadic outliers. Also, non-maximum-suppression and inertial information are used to decrease feature searching time. Consequently, a tightly coupled UKF fusion method is used to estimate ego-motion. The trifocal tensor geometry relationship between three consecutive images is used as measurement information which is wrapped into a RANSAC scheme to be robust against outliers. Therefore, the proposed method can handle well in dynamic environment. The experiments show the effectiveness of the proposed method in KITTI data which is a publicly available real world dataset.

articleTitle: Track Estimation and Maintenance for the BP-CBMeMBer Filter
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Aiming at the disadvantage that the box particle cardinality balanced multi-target multi-Bernoulli (BP-CBMeMBer) filter can not output the target tracks, a labeled BP-CBMeMBer (LBP-CBMeMBer) filter is proposed. First, each box particle is assigned a label, and the box particles sampled from the same target are assigned the same label. In this way, each label can be used as the identification of each target identity. Then, with the recursion of the filter, each label is transmitted in real time with each corresponding box particle. In the state estimation step, when the state of each target is estimated, the label of each target is also estimated together. Finally, the track of each target is formed by connecting the target states with the same label at different times. Simulation shows that the proposed filter can not only estimate the target number and target states, but also output the target tracks.

articleTitle: Stabilization of Switched Linear Systems via Observer-based Event-triggered Impulsive Control
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: This paper studies the event-triggered impulsive control problem of switched linear systems whose states are not available directly. An observer-based impulsive controller is designed to stabilize the concerned system. In order to achieve the desired performance, an observer-based impulsive controller and a mode-dependent event-triggered mechanism (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ETM$</tex>) are proposed. Some sufficient conditions are proposed and the control gains are designed. Moreover, the Zeno behavior can be excluded in our results. It is shown that a switched linear system can be efficiently stabilized by the observer-based impulsive controller under the mode-dependent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ETM$</tex> and arbitrary switching signal. Finally, a numerical example and its simulations are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed results.

articleTitle: Reduced-dimension beam-Doppler STAP method based on cross-correlation coefficient
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Reduced-dimension beam-Doppler STAP methods have reduced spatial and temporal dimension by spatial beamforming and temporal Doppler filtering. Firstly, this paper introduces the basic principle of the MCP and the MCC method proposed in this paper. Then, the reduced-dimension beam-Doppler Space-time adaptive processing is presented accordingly. Finally, the clutter suppression performance of different reduced-dimension beam-Doppler STAP methods are simulated and analyzed from two aspects, taper and beam number. While the taper gradually increasing or selecting specific auxiliary beam number, we conclude that the clutter suppression performance of the MCC or MCP method has its advantages, which provides theoretical basis for practical engineering application.

articleTitle: A new IMM interacting approach for unequal dimension states for multitarget tracking in cluttered environments
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Since it is unknown in advance whether the target is maneuvering in practical target tracking environments, multiple model tracking techniques are introduced by applying various target dynamic models. Among the multiple model tracking techniques, interacting multiple model (IMM) method has shown excellent performance with low complexity due to the interaction process of each state of mode. When various dynamic models are designed, the dimension of each state may be unequal, which may cause biased estimate. To deal with this problem, mode interacting approaches to two dynamic models of unequal dimensions have been studied in other literatures. Here, a new interacting approach for the case of three dynamic models with unequal dimensions is proposed to reduce the bias in the extra state estimates of the higher dimensional modes, and it is shown that the tracking performance is better than the existing IMM algorithm with the conventional interaction step through Monte Carlo simulation for multi-target tracking in cluttered environments.

articleTitle: Multi-sensor Bearings-only Target Tracking Using Two-stage Multiple Hypothesis Tracking
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The problem of multi-sensor bearings-only target tracking is addressed in this work. A practical challenge in this problem stems from the data association in dense clutter. In order to avoid the increase of computational complexity with the increase of the number of sensors and clutter density, a two-stage multiple hypothesis tracking (MHT) algorithm is proposed. First, the first stage MHT is performed at each local sensor, and the measurements with effective data association are sent to the fusion center. Second, the measurements from different sensors are combined and augmented to form new measurement vectors, which are then converted to Cartesian coordinates by iterated least squares (ILS) estimator. Therefore, in the second stage MHT, the Kalman filter can be used to update the target track. The performance of the two-stage MHT algorithm is illustrated with an example.

articleTitle: Design of radar waveform game platform based on PXI system
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In view of the lack of a test verification platform in the research of the game between radar and target, a test platform for radar waveform game is designed based on the PXI system. The platform includes a multi-channel radar and a simulator that can simulate targets and repeater jamming. The radar transmission waveform, signal processing, target and jamming parameters can be configured by the user, and it has good versatility. It provides a practical test and verification platform for radar waveform design and algorithm research under gaming conditions.

articleTitle: Pessimistic-optimistic multi-granularity decision rough set attribute reduction algorithm under incomplete relations
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The existing attribute reduction of single-granularity and multi-granularity decision-theoretic rough set are most carried out with an equivalence relationship under a complete information system. There are few researches focus on attribute reduction of incomplete information systems. At the same time, there is less research on new theoretical models such as pessimistic-optimistic multi-granularity decision rough sets. To make up the above shortcomings, this paper proposes a pessimistic-optimistic multi-granularity decision rough set model in an incomplete information system. The concepts of tolerance relation, attribute importance and approximate distribution quality are introduced into the model to form an attribute reduction algorithm under incomplete information system. It is proved by an example that the algorithm alleviates the limitation of multi-granularity decision rough set and makes the decision rough set not only limited to complete information systems and equivalence relations. Under this algorithm, the scope of application of multi-granularity decision rough sets and the accuracy of attribute reduction have been improved.

articleTitle: Kinematic and Dynamic Modeling of the PhantomX AX Metal Hexapod Mark III Robot using Quaternions
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: For years, hexapod robots have been the subject of study due to their many applications of use. Among their different characteristics, the great adaptability of locomotion and stability to hostile terrains are the main features that stand out the most. For that reason, it is fundamental to obtain its kinematic and dynamic model. For the development of its mathematical modeling, traditional spatial location tools are usually used, which leads to high computational costs, as well as a high complexity in its control system. In this context, this research developed the kinematic and dynamic modeling of the PhantomX AX Metal Hexapod Mark III Robot using quaternions; likewise, the modeling was carried out using the homogeneous transformation matrix for its comparison, both models were finally validated in a robotic simulation software CoppeliaSim. The RMSE was used as an error indicator, obtaining values not greater than 1.27 mm in the validation of the kinematics and values in the range of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> Nm in the validation of the dynamics, showing that both models were valid. One of the most important conclusions is that an adaptation of Newton Euler's algorithm for the calculation of dynamics using quaternions is obtained, applied to different types of open kinematic chain robots. Finally, the computational cost of the models using quaternions and the homogeneous transformation matrix was compared, a reduction of 21.4% was obtained with the use of quaternions in kinematic modeling; however, in dynamic modeling with Newton Euler, a reduction of 27% was obtained with the use of homogeneous transformation matrices.

articleTitle: A Design of Food Storage Auxiliary Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Refrigerators are an essential element of modern life, but they are also a health threat. Due to the huge variety of food in refrigerators and different food spoilage cycles, users tend to miss the safe consumption period. In this paper, we present the design of a food storage auxiliary monitoring device, which is divided into two main parts, the master unit and the slave unit. The main unit with display is installed at the periphery of the refrigerator and embedded with a database of typical food spoilage cycles based on temperature, humidity and seasonal factors. The slave, on the other hand, is a simplified version of the main unit, with no display mounted on the main aisle. Users can use voice recognition to enter or delete categories of food when storing food. When a person passes by the host or extension, the device is triggered and will perform different frequency of voice alerts according to the life span of the food. User can also customize the food spoilage cycle at the smart terminal according to the actual situation. The hardware, software and communication design scheme of the device is proposed in the paper, and the accuracy of speech recognition is tested to be as high as 97%, which verifies its reliability and feasibility. Meanwhile, the device can be used as a voice note or voice reminder.

articleTitle: Medical image feature extraction and visualization based on principal component analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In view of the problem that it is difficult to extract and analyze the medical image feature information, this paper investigates a feature extraction and visualization method of medical image based on principal component analysis. Firstly, the medical image feature extraction and space conversion mechanism is analyzed, and the feature information from the original spatial dimensions of medical images is extracted by using PCA technology. Then the extracted feature image is effectively reconstructed and visualized. The method is verification through COVID-19 CT images, results show that when the cumulative contribution rate of the principal component reaches 85%, the principal component analysis method can restore the information of the original image more clearly, and realize the feature extraction and visual reconstruction of medical images.

articleTitle: Domain Adaptation for Viewpoint Estimation with Image Generation
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Viewpoint estimation is the pre-procedure for purposive perception and fine pose estimation, which has vital applications in robot manipulation and grasping. Unfortunately, the viewpoint estimation task is usually affected by a lack of training data with accurate annotations. In this paper, the problem of viewpoint estimation for untextured workpiece images is handled with the help of image translation and unsupervised domain adaptation. To augment the dataset, we transfer the 3D-rendering CAD images to the real-like images, which are visually similar to the real images, by utilizing a novel shape-constraint image generation model. Inspired by the ability of domain adaptation to bridge the domain gap, the distributions of these real-like images with real workpiece images are aligned by jointly optimizing the Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) and H-divergence. Experiments show that our framework can achieve better authenticity for image translation, and improvements of the viewpoint estimation can be fulfilled over all the workpiece types, without the need of viewpoint labels of real workpiece images for training.

articleTitle: DBLD-SLAM: A Deep-Learning Visual SLAM System Based on Deep Binary Local Descriptor
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The feature quality is critical for positioning accuracy of feature-descriptor-matching-based visual SLAM (Visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping). State-of-the-art handcrafted descriptors like BRIEF and ORB can hardly work well in complex scenarios. On the other hand, CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) is proved to have tremendous advantages on image feature extraction. In this paper, we develop a CNN model to extract binary visual feature descriptor from image patches with four important loss functions, namely adaptive scale loss, even distribution loss, quantization loss and correlation loss. Based on this learned deep binary feature descriptor sharing the same structure with ORB descriptor, a monocular SLAM system named DBLD-SLAM is designed, by replacing the ORB descriptor in conventional ORB-SLAM. We also train visual Bag of Words to detect loop closure. Experiments show that our DBLD descriptor achieves better results on the HPatches dataset and UBC benchmark. Moreover, the DBLD-SLAM system outperforms other current popular SLAM system on Tartanair dataset.

articleTitle: Deadline-based V2V Charging Under Spatial Resource Constraints
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Electric Vehicle (EV) becomes a mainstream transportation tool in recent years as it is environmentally friendly and energy-usage effectively. However, due to the inconvenience of EV charging, EV requires charging optimization to improve its Quality of Experience (QoE). Previous researches focus on EV's plug-in charging mode (EVs drive to charging station for energy supplement), but it has spatial limitations (fixed location and charging station operation cost). With the development of charging technology, a Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) charging mode is proposed as a replacement for plug-in mode. Here, EVs are divided into Charging EVs (C-EVs) and Discharging EVs (D-EVs). D-EVs can transfer their surplus energy to C-EVs. This V2V mode not only avoids the limitation of charging location, but also provides EVs with more flexibility in the temporal domain (avoids charging congestion). In this paper, a deadline-based V2V charging scheme is proposed. Through the aggregated information of EVs (location and energy supply/demand) and Parking Lots (PLs), V2V charging-discharging pairs (V2V-Pairs) are matched by the Global Controller (GC). Furthermore, an appropriate PL is selected for the V2V charging operation. We simulate the V2V mode in Helsinki City scenario under constrained spatial parking resources, and the results show that the proposed V2V charging scheme has better charging efficiency.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Measurement Converted KF, EKF, UKF, CKF, and PF in GMTI Filtering
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The ground moving target indicator (GMTI) radar plays an important role in surveillance, precision tracking, and classification of ground moving targets. The measurements of a GMTI radar are range, azimuth, and radial velocity, which are nonlinear functions of the Cartesian target and sensor states. In our 2003 SPIE paper we analyzed the performance of the converted measurement based Kalman filter (CMKF), extended Kalman filter (EKF), unscented Kalman filter (UKF), and transition density based particle filter (TD-PF). In this paper, we extend our previous work by considering the cubature Kalman filter (CKF). We also compute the posterior Cramér-Rao lower bound (PCRLB) to judge the accuracy of the filters relative to the best achievable accuracy. The results of this analysis are useful in an operational system where a filter has to chosen based on state estimation accuracy, scalability, and computational complexity. We also analyze the accuracy of the TD-PF by varying the number of particles. We perform Monte Carlo simulations to analyze the accuracy and computational complexity of various filters. Based on the root time-averaged mean square (RTAMS) error of position and velocity, we find that the CMKF, EKF, UKF, and CKF have nearly the same accuracy in cases analyzed. To achieve the same level of accuracy, the TD-PF requires more than 40,000 particles with about 508 times more computational cost relative to the EKF. Contrary to conventional thinking, our results show that for cases analyzed the EKF produces the best accuracy with stable performance and lowest computational cost.

articleTitle: A Mobile Robotic Arm Grasping System with Autonomous Navigation and Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a mobile robotic arm grasping system suitable for various service requirements in indoor environments. For the task of grasping the given object, both the navigation and the visual recognition positioning are prerequisite. In order to realize the robot's autonomous navigation, the use of Cartographer algorithm is employed to build an unknown environment map. To improve the grasping quality, we develop a grasping system that uses YOLOv4 combined with the GrabCut algorithm for the robotic arm, which can be applied to various objects in different scenarios. First, the YOLOv4 algorithm is introduced to identify and locate the individual objects. Secondly, the output frame can be used as an input of the GrabCut algorithm to segment the objects from the background for calculating the capture orientation. Thirdly, the conversion between the coordinate systems is conducted to acquire the positions of objects, and the obtained information is sent to the robotic arm to complete the grasping task on the Robot Operating System (ROS). The experimental results show that the grasping success rate with the proposed algorithm is close to 92.2%, which is of great significance to the application of in home service robot scenario.

articleTitle: Human Gait Classification Based on Convolutional Neural Network using Interferometric Radar
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Doppler radars are capable of measuring the micro-Doppler signatures of a walking person for human gait analysis. However, when the person's trajectory is approaching 60° away from radar antenna broadside, the micro-Doppler signatures due to radial velocity diminish significantly, thus providing insufficient information for classification. To resolve this issue, we propose a new algorithm for human gait classification based on convolutional neural network (CNN) using interferometric radar. We implement the classification algorithm based on dual micro-motion signatures using interferometric radar which allows the measurement of both the interferometric and micro-Doppler signatures due to the angular and radial velocities of the walking person, respectively. Three human gait classes including full arm motion (FAM), partial arm motion (PAM) and no arm motion (NAM) at two different angles between the radar antennas baseline and direction of motion are considered for dataset generation. Time-varying Doppler and interferometric spectrograms are fed as input to train CNN. Simulation results validate the fact that the proposed classification algorithm using interferometric radar enhances the performance of human gait classification algorithm in terms of accuracy and robustness, regardless of the trajectory.

articleTitle: Space-oriented Label Partitioning for Multi-object Tracking
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The problem of tracking multiple objects has been investigated in various research and industrial fields. Among existing methods, random finite set (RFS) solutions such as the generalized labeled multi-Bernoulli (GLMB) filter has provided efficient solutions with solid theoretical justifications. Furthermore, implementations show that the GLMB approach is efficient under challenging scenarios. In this paper, we study an RFS-based method for multi-object tracking (MOT) through a simple data structure for label partitioning. Specifically, grid index structure based techniques for splitting a label space and a label-partitioned GLMB tracker are investigated. We finally evaluate the performance of label partitioning and the GLMB filter via various means such as visualization, execution time, and MOT metrics.

articleTitle: State Estimation with Linear Equality Constraints Based on Trajectory Function of Time and Karush-Kuhn-Tucker Conditions
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In this paper, we address the constrained target tracking problem based on the approach of the trajectory function of time, in which the target state satisfies equality constraints. What is different from the previous work is that we handle equality constraints by means of utilizing Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions within the trajectory curve fitting framework. A simple numerical example has been used for demonstrating the advantage of our proposed approach in comparison with the exiting Kalman filter based on the projection approach and the pseudo-observation approach.

articleTitle: IMM-CKF for a Highly Maneuvering Target Using Converted Measurements
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: We consider the state estimation of a highly maneuvering aircraft using an air moving target indicator (AMTI) radar. The AMTI radar measures the range, azimuth, and radial velocity of the target. In our previous work, we used the interacting multiple model (IMM) filter with the extended Kalman filter (EKF), unscented Kalman filter (UKF), and cubature Kalman filter (CKF) using the AMTI measurements. In this paper, we use the converted measurements in an IMM-CKF and analyze the performances of these two types of algorithms. The converted measurements include the unbiased converted measurement (UCM) and modified unbiased converted measurement (MUCM) or conditional mean. The performances of the filters are analyzed using the root mean square position and velocity errors, root time-averaged mean square (RTAMS) error, average normalized estimation error squared (ANEES), mode probabilities, and computational cost. We also compute the posterior Cramér-Rao lower bound to evaluate these two types of algorithms.

articleTitle: MIMO Radar Waveform Design with Desirable Beampattern and Controllable Power Uniformity
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In this paper, the problem of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar transmit waveform design is considered. Specifically, aiming at the insufficiency of the peak-to-average-power ratio (PAR) constraint in controlling the transmit power uniformity across the array, we introduce a new waveform constraint, namely, peak-to-valley-power-ratio (PVR) constraint to directly control the transmit power dynamic range. The proposed PVR constraint is capable of keeping the transmit power of each antenna within an allowable range of power difference, which apparently enables to improve the power efficiency of the radar system. We then formulate a fractional cost function that minimizes the integrated sidelobe level (ISL) and simultaneously maximizes the energy in the mainlobe subject to the PVR constraint and the mainlobe ripple constraint (MRC). To solve the resultant non-linear and non-convex problem, we propose an efficient iterative method in the ADMM framework. Numerical examples are provided to demonstrate the superiority of the proposed algorithm over several existing methods in terms of low sidelobe levels and mainlobe ripple control.

articleTitle: Probability Hypothesis Density Filter Visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
